title: Total-limit transport of the scalar-extended exceptional counit word
statement:
Fix $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ of characteristic $p$, a prime $\ell\ne p$, and finite extensions $E\subset L$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation rings $R=\mathcal O_E$, $S=\mathcal O_L$, uniformizers $\pi,v$, and ramification index $e\ge1$, so $\pi S=v^eS$. Put $A_n=R/\pi^n$, $B_n=S/\pi^nS=S/v^{en}$, for $n\ge1$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber, def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $f:X\to Y$ be a separated finite-type morphism of separated finite-type $k$-schemes, with a fixed compactification $f=pj$, $j$ open and $p$ proper [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties, def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support]. Work on fixed small pro-etale skeletons [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-size-convention]. For $D=R,S$ and $W=X,Y$, let $\mathscr N_D(W)$ be the full subcategory of the ordinary unbounded derived category of strict semilinear systems over $(A_n)_W$ or $(B_n)_W$ consisting of normalized systems with levels in $D^b_{ctf}$ [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus, def-coef-normalized-dvr-tower, def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude, def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility]. Normalized means that every transition-adjoint $N_m\otimes^L_{A_m}A_n\to N_n$, or its $B$ analogue, is invertible for $m\ge n$. Write $\mathsf F_D\dashv\mathsf E_D$ for the specified compact-support/exceptional system adjunction, and $\epsilon_D^{\rm sys}$ for its counit, with the simultaneous enriched realizations of [lem-coef-finite-adjunction-diagram-realization, lem-coef-cartesian-section-adjoint-mates]. The $S$ functors here are retained at the levels $en$, with composite quotient transitions.

Use completed coefficient sheaves and derived-complete bounded constructible categories $\mathcal C_D(W)$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients, def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed]. Let $M\in\mathcal C_R(Y)$, $N=\mathcal R_{R,Y}M$, where $\mathcal R_R$ is coherent reduction, and let $\mathcal L_S^{(e)}$ be total derived limit on the retained $B_n$ systems [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus]. Use $T_W=-\widehat\otimes_R^LS$ [def-weil-integral-scalar-extension], the integral adjunctions $F_D=Rf_{!,D}\dashv G_D=Rf_D^!$ with counits $\epsilon_D$ [prop-coef-integral-exceptional-adjoint], and the system scalar functor and canonical $\alpha^{\rm sys}$ of [lem-coef-ramified-scalar-system-transpose]. Let $\alpha:T_YF_R\xrightarrow{\sim}F_ST_X$ be its total-limit comparison, with the finite-free compact-support normalization [lem-pur-compact-support-integral-coefficient-comparison]. Use the canonical source, intermediate and target identifications, including cofinality and the completed-scalar comparison $\chi$, of [lem-coef-ramified-scalar-exceptional-limit].

For the natural system morphism
$$\lambda_N=\mathsf T_Y^{(e)}(\epsilon^{\rm sys}_{R,N})\circ(\alpha^{\rm sys}_{\mathsf E_RN})^{-1}:
\mathsf F_S\mathsf T_X^{(e)}\mathsf E_RN\longrightarrow\mathsf T_Y^{(e)}N,$$
its total limit satisfies the following equality of natural integral maps:
$$\mathcal L_{S,Y}^{(e)}(\lambda_N)
=T_Y(\epsilon_{R,M})\circ\alpha_{G_RM}^{-1}:
F_ST_XG_RM\longrightarrow T_YM.$$
In this formula the left-hand side is conjugated by the specified endpoint identifications. In particular, the limit of $\mathsf T_Y^{(e)}(\epsilon^{\rm sys}_{R,N})$ is $T_Y(\epsilon_{R,M})$, including the intermediate reconstruction-counit comparison for $\mathsf F_R\mathsf E_RN$. The identification uses the actual normalized reduction/limit unit and counit, so it is compatible with the descended integral adjunction of [lem-pur-normalized-reconstruction-adjunction-calculus]. This equality holds as a natural transformation constructed before finite projections are taken; no faithfulness of finite evaluation on morphisms is assumed. It includes the identity extension $E=L$, identity morphism $f$, zero input, and empty source or target, with their canonical identity or zero maps.

proof.text:
Write $\mathcal R=\mathcal R_R$, $\mathcal L=\mathcal L_R$, and $u,e$ for their actual unit and counit; write $\mathsf F=\mathsf F_R$, $\mathsf E=\mathsf E_R$. Put $h=\epsilon^{\rm sys}_{R,N}:P=\mathsf F\mathsf EN\to N$. The reconstruction-adjunction calculus, restricted to the constructible subcategories, gives the intermediate comparison and counit formula
$$\kappa=\mathcal L_Y\mathsf F(e_{\mathsf EN}):F_RG_RM\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal L_YP,\qquad
\epsilon_{R,M}=u_M^{-1}\circ\mathcal L_Y(h)\circ\kappa.$$
The descended-counit lemma identifies the counit $\epsilon_{R,M}$ of the specified adjunction of the integral exceptional-adjoint node with exactly this descended formula, as an equality of integral maps; no adjunction map is chosen from an objectwise reconstruction or inferred from finite reductions. The integral exceptional-adjoint node specifies the coherent realization $G_R=\mathcal L_X\mathsf E\mathcal R_Y$; the limit-identification node supplies its constructible domain, uniform Tor intervals, and the canonical intermediate identification. Thus the displayed formula applies to this $M$ and to these operations.

source.place: paragraph 8, adjunction evaluations and counits; explicit reduction/limit descent

proof.text:
Set $B=\mathcal L_{S,Y}^{(e)}\mathsf T_Y^{(e)}$, and denote the specified natural scalar-limit identification by $\rho_K:B\mathcal R_YK\xrightarrow{\sim}T_YK$. For the normalized systems used here write
$$\sigma_Q=B(e_Q)\circ\rho_{\mathcal L_YQ}^{-1}:T_Y\mathcal L_YQ\xrightarrow{\sim}BQ.$$
This just expresses the scalar comparison on a reconstructed system using its actual reconstruction counit. The canonical intermediate endpoint for $BP$ in the question is consequently
$$d_P=T_Y(\kappa^{-1})\circ\sigma_P^{-1}:BP\xrightarrow{\sim}T_YF_RG_RM,$$
and the endpoint for $BN$ is $\rho_M$. These are precisely the prescribed comparisons: the limit-identification node specifies the comparisons on functors and morphisms using $\chi$, cofinality, and the actual reconstruction maps. The reconstruction calculus gives the composition comparison $\kappa$ and naturality of $e$; no separate comparison of their finite evaluations is used.

source.place: paragraph 8, finite free coefficient tensor and derived limit; intermediate reconstruction endpoint

proof.text:
Apply naturality of the reconstruction counit to $h:P\to N$:
$$h\circ e_P=e_N\circ\mathcal R_Y\mathcal L_Y(h).$$
Naturality of $\rho$ at $\mathcal L_Y(h)$ therefore gives
$$B(h)\circ\sigma_P=B(e_N)\circ\rho_{\mathcal L_YN}^{-1}\circ T_Y\mathcal L_Y(h).$$
Since $N=\mathcal R_YM$, the triangle identity says $e_N\circ\mathcal R_Y(u_M)=1_N$. Naturality of $\rho$ at $u_M$ then gives
$$\rho_M\circ B(e_N)\circ\rho_{\mathcal L_YN}^{-1}=T_Y(u_M^{-1}).$$
Substitute this equality and the definition of $d_P^{-1}=\sigma_P\circ T_Y(\kappa)$ into the preceding equation. Functoriality yields
$$\rho_M\circ B(h)\circ d_P^{-1}
=T_Y(u_M^{-1}\circ\mathcal L_Y(h)\circ\kappa)
=T_Y(\epsilon_{R,M}).$$
This proves the asserted scalar-counit identification including its intermediate reconstruction comparison; every cancellation occurred in the whole-system or integral categories.

source.place: paragraph 8, counits preserved by coefficient comparisons; naturality and triangle-identity calculation

proof.text: The system-transpose node supplies the actual natural isomorphism $\alpha^{\rm sys}_{\mathsf EN}$ and the system word $\lambda_N=\mathsf T_Y^{(e)}(h)\circ(\alpha^{\rm sys}_{\mathsf EN})^{-1}$. Under the prescribed source and intermediate endpoints, the limit-identification node identifies $\mathcal L_{S,Y}^{(e)}(\alpha^{\rm sys}_{\mathsf EN})$ with $\alpha_{G_RM}$. A functor sends an inverse to the inverse of its image: apply it to the two inverse identities. Consequently the conjugated limit of $(\alpha^{\rm sys}_{\mathsf EN})^{-1}$ is $\alpha_{G_RM}^{-1}$, with the same intermediate endpoint $d_P$ as in step 3.

source.place: paragraph 8, compact-support finite-free normalization and adjunction formula

proof.text:
Apply total-limit functoriality to the displayed composite defining $\lambda_N$, and insert the inverse pair of intermediate identifications $d_P^{-1}d_P$. Steps 3 and 4 give
$$\mathcal L_{S,Y}^{(e)}(\lambda_N)=T_Y(\epsilon_{R,M})\circ\alpha_{G_RM}^{-1}.$$
All units, counits and scalar comparisons in the calculation are natural transformations, so the calculation is natural in $M$ before finite projections. It never uses faithfulness of those projections. For $E=L$, the identity scalar comparison gives the same formula for the original counit; for $f=1$, the identity adjunction gives the identity scalar map. A zero input gives zero objects and maps. For empty $X$ the compact-support source is zero; for empty $Y$ the existence of $f$ forces $X$ empty as well. Thus the same calculation includes all the stated boundary cases.
